mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates restrictive monetary policy that suppresses corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to lower equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 20d forward returns is negative and statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 5d forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: The interaction effect (joint decline) fails to produce negative returns in more than 50% of cases, with a Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1% in a month signals a supply shock that disrupts corporate supply chains and reduces earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% in the current month
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where INDPRO falls > 1% in a month, the S&P 500 produces positive 20d forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS against 5d forward returns is positive and statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 60d forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units and real GDP (GDPC1) below 16000 billion dollars signal a severe demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST < 1400 and GDPC1 < 16000) fails to produce negative returns in more than 50% of cases, with a Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.25 percentage points signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines > 0.25pp in the current month
failure_condition: In more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines > 0.25pp in a month, the S&P 500 produces negative 5d forward returns.
